99at.% Fe-1at.% Zr was mechanically alloyed from elemental powders via high-energy ball milling in a SPEX 8000 shaker mill. Milling vials were carefully prepared in an ultra-high purity argon atmosphere to avoid excessive oxygen contamination. Milling was performed for 24 hours with a 10:1 ball to powder mass ratio.
Samples were annealed in a standard tube furnace with an Ar-2% H2 gas mixture. Milling and annealing procedures were the same as described in Reference 19.

evidence.quote: By using the {100} forbidden reflections in Fig. 2A to obtain a TEM dark field (DF) image, the morphology, size, and distribution of the superlattice regions reveal a random dispersion of equiaxed nano-clusters with a size range of 2–5 nm, as shown in Fig. 2B.

A Zr elemental map in the Fe-1at.% Zr sample, recorded in STEM/EDS (Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy/Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy) mode with a probe size of 1 nm, is presented in Fig. 4A. The blue regions (Zr-enriched) are found to be about 5 nm, the same as the size of the NSS clusters revealed by a dark-field image in Fig. S3B, which indicates enrichment of Zr in the clusters.

The EELS results revealed that surface oxides existed on both the Fe-1at.%Zr and unalloyed Fe TEM samples, which has the structure of Spinel Fe3O4 as identified by selected area electron diffraction (SAED)
Based on the above observations, we propose the NSS clusters with a D03 (A3B) structure, where Fe occupies the A sites and O occupies the B sites to form a Fe3O unit cell (Fig. 5A).
